data.question_title: 1.0gm of a mixture NaCl and anhydrous \(\text{Na\({}_{2}\)CO\({}_{3}\)}\) is exactly neutralized by 50ml of \(\cfrac{N}{5} \)solution of an acid. The percentage of NaCl in the mixture is
data.explanation_txt:
50 ml of N/5 acid = 10 ml of 1N acid (in terms of quantity) 

No. of gram equivalent of acid = 0.01

Amount of Na\(_2\)CO\(_3\) that is dissolved by the acid = 0.01 \(\times\) Equivalent Weight of Na\(_2\)CO\(_3\) = 0.01*53 = 0.53 gm

\(\therefore\) Percentage of NaCl in the mixture = \(\cfrac{1-0.53}{1}\times 100 \% = 47\%\)

data.question_title:
Primitive man was probably mainly concerned with fire as a source of warmth and as a means for cooking food than as a source of light. Before he discovered less laborious ways of making fire, he had to preserve it, and whenever he went on a journey he carried a fire brand with him. His discovery that the firebrand, from which the torch may very well have developed, could be used for illumination was probably incidental to the primary purpose of preserving a flame.

Lamps, too, probably developed by accident. Early man has had his first conception of a lamp While watching a twig or fiber burning in molten fat dropped from a roasting carcass. all he had to do was to fasten a vessel to contain fat and float a lighted reed in it, which were made of hollowed stones or sea shells, have persisted in identical from up to quite recent times.
